dfd.title: DFD Editor
dfd.description: Create and edit your Data Flow Diagram here.

autoNumbering.diagonalHint: Score = weightX·x + weightY·y. The element closest to the top-left corner wins. Configurable weights, IdLabel position as tiebreaker.
autoNumbering.topDownHint: Elements higher up get lower numbers. Within the same row (tolerance band), left wins. Best for document-style DFDs.
autoNumbering.leftRightHint: Elements further left get lower numbers. Within the same column (tolerance band), top wins. Best for OT/ICS diagrams with field–control–IT zones.
autoNumbering.toleranceHintX: Maximum X-distance (px) for two elements to be treated as the same column. Top wins within the band.
autoNumbering.toleranceHintY: Maximum Y-distance (px) for two elements to be treated as the same row. Left wins within the band.
autoNumbering.weightsHint: Score = weightX·x + weightY·y. Higher Y weight → vertical position matters more. Default: 0.8x + 1.0y.
autoNumbering.configHint: Click Auto-Number after saving to apply. All elements will be renumbered from scratch.

validation.atLeastOneSecurityGoal: At least one security goal required

label.unknownVerb: {{detail}} — unknown verb "{{verb}}" (valid: pull, push, write, read, stream)
label.synonymVerb: {{detail}} — "{{verb}}" not permitted; use 'pull' instead of fetch/query, 'push' instead of emit/notify/publish/receive
label.multipleTags: {{detail}} — only one [flow-type] tag allowed per flow (found: {{tags}})
label.objectEmbeddedVerb: {{detail}} — object must not start with a verb (found: "{{verb}}"); use a domain-oriented noun instead

label_property.electrical_pull_verb: Protocol conflict — '{{protocol}}' is unidirectional, pull is not applicable
label_property.write_target_not_datastore: Invalid write target — '{{targetName}}' is a {{targetType}}, expected DataStore
label_property.read_source_not_datastore: Invalid read source — '{{sourceName}}' is a {{sourceType}}, expected DataStore
label_property.read_on_communication_store: Invalid read — '{{storeName}}' is an active service (accessModel: communication); use pull [req]/[resp]
label_property.read_store_unclassified: '{{storeName}}' has no accessModel/technology — classify the store before using read
label_property.pull_on_direct_access_store: '{{storeName}}' is passive storage (accessModel: direct_access) — consider read instead of pull

pull.missingResponse: {{detail}} — no matching pull [resp] found for this pull [req]
pull.multipleResponses: {{detail}} — multiple pull [resp] found, expected exactly one
pull.orphanedResponse: {{detail}} — orphaned pull [resp], no matching pull [req] found

write.redundantFlowType: {{detail}} — write must not carry a flow-type or annotation (found: [{{flowType}}])

read.redundantFlowType: {{detail}} — read must not carry a flow-type or annotation (found: [{{flowType}}])

stream.invalidFlowType: {{detail}} — invalid flow-type "{{flowType}}" for stream (only [stream] is allowed, or omit entirely)
stream.logicalAnnotationForbidden: {{detail}} — stream flows may not use logical annotations ([{{flowType}}] is semantically incompatible with stream)

reqResp.duplicateCoverage: {{detail}} — [req_resp] coexists with {{conflictDisplayId}} "{{conflictDetail}}" on the same interaction; remove one to avoid duplicate threat coverage

eventAck.duplicateCoverage: {{detail}} — [event_ack] coexists with {{conflictDisplayId}} "{{conflictDetail}}" on the same flow; remove one to avoid duplicate threat coverage

object.forbiddenTerm: {{detail}} — object contains a transport or encoding term ({{terms}}); use a domain-oriented name instead

prop.bidirectionalForbidden: {{detail}} — bidirectional flows are forbidden, model as two unidirectional flows
prop.pullNotReqResp: {{detail}} — pull requires direction 'Request-Response', update the Direction property
prop.pushIsReqResp: {{detail}} — push is fire-and-forget, 'Request-Response' direction contradicts push semantics
prop.pushWrongDirection: {{detail}} — push requires direction 'Uni-directional', update the Direction property
prop.writeIsReqResp: {{detail}} — write is a one-way operation, 'Request-Response' direction contradicts write semantics
prop.writeNotDatastore: {{detail}} — write with non-datastore protocol, verify flow targets a Data Store (expected: database or file)
prop.streamNotContinuous: {{detail}} — stream requires continuous frequency, update the Frequency property
prop.streamIsReqResp: {{detail}} — stream is unidirectional, 'Request-Response' direction is unexpected for stream
prop.continuousUseStream: {{detail}} — continuous push/pull detected, consider using 'stream' instead
prop.excludeMissingRationale: DataFlow {{detail}} — excluded from threat generation without rationale — add an exclusion rationale for IEC 62443-4-1 audit trail
prop.protocolMissing: {{detail}} — transport protocol not specified; treat as unknown/highest risk for threat analysis
prop.readIsReqResp: {{detail}} — read is direct storage access, 'Request-Response' direction contradicts read semantics

tls.noTerminator: {{detail}}: flow uses TLS but neither endpoint terminates it. Set tlsTermination (server or mutual) on the terminating process.
tls.mtlsRequiresBothMutual: {{detail}}: mutual TLS requires both endpoints to be mutual-capable. Set tlsTermination=mutual on both processes.
tls.handshakeMismatch: {{detail}}: one endpoint requires mutual TLS while the other cannot present a client certificate. Align tlsTermination on both endpoints.

exposure_level.label: Exposure Level
exposure_level.below_tb_hint: Below Trust Boundary EL — override requires rationale
exposure_level.rationale_placeholder: Why does this differ from the Trust Boundary EL?
exposure_level.el0_description: Inside the machine enclosure, no external access possible
exposure_level.el1_description: Physical access required (USB, serial port, locked cabinet)
exposure_level.el3_description: Industrial factory network, VPN or partner / OT network

physical_exposure_level.pel0_description: PEL0 – Inaccessible: No practical physical access without destruction — potted, welded, or chip-decap required. No meaningful attack surface from physical side.
physical_exposure_level.pel1_description: PEL1 – Deep Internal: Multiple physical barriers must be overcome — e.g. JTAG behind two nested enclosures, or inside a locked sub-module inside a locked cabinet.
physical_exposure_level.pel2_description: PEL2 – Internal: One physical barrier to bypass — open enclosure, unlock cabinet, remove screws. Tool or key access required. e.g. LAN port inside device housing.
physical_exposure_level.pel3_description: PEL3 – Surface Accessible: Externally reachable without opening anything, but not directly usable — e.g. a service flap that must be opened, a recessed port behind a cover. No tool required.
physical_exposure_level.pel4_description: PEL4 – Directly Exposed: No physical barrier — touchscreen, outdoor USB, card reader. Directly reachable by anyone. Combine with PB.accessibility for environmental context.

cascade_hints.usb: USB interfaces are a common attack surface on embedded systems. Consider setting Safety Relevant if this interface is connected to safety-critical components.
cascade_hints.serial: Serial interfaces are often connected to debug consoles or safety-critical components. Consider setting Safety Relevant if applicable.
cascade_hints.gpio: GPIO pins may be directly connected to safety actuators or sensors. Consider setting Safety Relevant if this interface controls or reads safety-critical hardware.
cascade_hints.uart: UART is frequently used as an unprotected debug console or configuration interface. Ensure access is restricted in production.
cascade_hints.rs232: RS-232 interfaces often allow diagnostic or configuration access. Physical access controls are recommended.
cascade_hints.rs485: RS-485 / Modbus is common in safety-critical industrial systems. Set Safety Relevant if actuators or sensors are connected.
cascade_hints.can: CAN Bus has no built-in authentication or encryption. Set Safety Relevant if used in automotive or industrial safety systems.
cascade_hints.analog_in: Analog inputs are connected to physical sensors. Manipulation of signal levels can falsify measurements. Consider Safety Relevant.
cascade_hints.analog_out: Analog outputs control actuators. Manipulation of output signals can have safety-critical consequences. Set Safety Relevant.
cascade_hints.jtag: JTAG provides full CPU debug access including memory R/W and flash programming. This port must be locked or disabled in production.
cascade_hints.swd: SWD provides ARM debug and flash programming access. This port must be locked or disabled in production. Set Safety Relevant if safety-critical firmware is affected.

tooltips.ethernet: Wired Ethernet (10/100/1000 Mbps, PoE). Physical connection required.
tooltips.wifi: IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi. No physical access required — remotely reachable.
tooltips.bluetooth: Bluetooth Classic / BLE. No physical access required.
tooltips.fiber: Fibre optic. Physical tap requires cable interruption.
tooltips.uart: UART/USART — frequently an unprotected debug console port. High risk.
tooltips.rs232: RS-232 point-to-point serial. Common in legacy industrial equipment.
tooltips.rs485: RS-485 / Modbus RTU. Multi-drop bus — any device on the bus can read data.
tooltips.can: CAN Bus — no authentication or encryption by default. Automotive and industrial.
tooltips.i2c: I²C — short-range bus to sensors, EEPROMs, and peripherals. PCB access required.
tooltips.spi: SPI — high-speed bus to peripherals. PCB access required.
tooltips.lin: LIN Bus — single-wire, low speed. Automotive body/chassis.
tooltips.usb: USB (any class). Risk: DFU mode, HID injection (BadUSB), mass storage.
tooltips.jtag: Full JTAG: CPU halt, memory R/W, flash read/write. Highest debug risk.
tooltips.swd: ARM Serial Wire Debug — comparable capabilities to JTAG. Lock in production.
tooltips.swd_swo: SWD + SWO (Single Wire Output) — debug access plus lightweight ITM trace.
tooltips.jtag_trace: JTAG + ETM Trace Port — full debug access plus instruction trace.
tooltips.gpio: General Purpose I/O. Risk depends on function.
tooltips.analog_in: Analog Input (ADC) — sensor or signal input. Manipulation affects measurements.
tooltips.analog_out: Analog Output (DAC) — actuator or signal output. Safety-critical in many systems.
tooltips.pwm: PWM Output — motor control, dimming. Safety-relevant for actuators.
tooltips.touchscreen: Local touch HMI — operator interaction surface. Requires physical presence; model protection against unauthorized local operation on the target Process.

location.label: Physical Location
location.placeholder: e.g. server room, production floor, field cabinet

tooltips.on_chip: Internal chip pad or register — EL0, debug interface only
tooltips.in_enclosure: Port inside sealed enclosure — EL1, requires disassembly
tooltips.external_panel: Panel-mounted port on device exterior — EL1

tooltips.enabled: Fully active — full threat surface applies
tooltips.enabled_read_only: Output only, no input accepted (e.g. UART log-only mode). Command injection path eliminated.
tooltips.sw_disabled: Disabled via config or firmware — reversible without hardware access. Residual risk: re-enable via software exploit.
tooltips.hw_disabled: Disabled via jumper or DIP switch — requires physical access to re-enable. Lower residual risk.
tooltips.permanent_disabled: Irreversibly disabled — OTP fuse blown, pad unpopulated, or epoxy-filled. No threats generated.

connectorType.label: Connector Type
connectorType.not_applicable: Not applicable for this interface type

safetyRelevant.label: Safety-relevant interface (EN 50742 — e.g. programming port on Safety PLC)

safetyRationale.label: Safety Rationale
safetyRationale.placeholder: e.g. Direct access to safety-critical programming interface

description.label: Description
description.helperText: Who or what is this external entity?

authorizationScope.label: Authorization Scope
authorizationScope.placeholder: e.g., Read-only, Specific endpoints, Limited operations

stride_hint.title: STRIDE Relevance: S (Spoofing), R (Repudiation)
stride_hint.description: External entities are outside your control. Enforce strong authentication, least privilege, and non-repudiation.

trust_boundary_warning.title: This data flow crosses a Trust Boundary!
trust_boundary_warning.hint: High risk for: Tampering, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service

excludeFromThreatGen.label: Exclude from automated threat generation
excludeFromThreatGen.warning_no_trust: Excluding a flow without marking it as Assumed Trusted may hide real threats. Add a trust rationale above.

excludeFromThreatGenRationale.label: Exclusion Rationale (IEC 62443-4-1 audit trail)
excludeFromThreatGenRationale.placeholder: e.g. Internal sensor polling within trusted safety domain, no external access path exists
excludeFromThreatGenRationale.error: Rationale required for IEC 62443-4-1 audit trail

electrical.not_applicable_hint: Hardwired signal — encryption and endpoint authentication are not applicable. Physical access to the wiring is the primary attack vector.
electrical.physical_boundary_warning: Hardwired signal crosses a Trust Boundary — physical wire access is the attack vector. Consider: cable routing, tamper seals, terminal access control.

noTransportMedium.context_hint: No transport medium for this protocol — routing and redundancy do not apply.
noTransportMedium.not_applicable_hint: No transport medium — exposure level, encryption and endpoint authentication do not apply. Protection against unauthorized use lives on the target process.

encryptionInTransit.label: Encryption in Transit
encryptionInTransit.warning: Unencrypted flow crosses trust boundary → Information Disclosure risk

integrityProtection.label: Integrity Protection

options.crc: CRC — detects errors, NOT targeted manipulation

integrityProtection.tooltip: How is the integrity of data in transit protected? Modbus RTU CRC = 'crc' — present but NOT cryptographic. Only HMAC and Signature protect against targeted MITM manipulation.

location.label: Physical Medium / Routing

options.field_cable: Field cable (M12, DIN rail, cable duct)

location.tooltip: Physical medium or routing path this flow traverses. Determines DoS attack vectors: field_cable → plug-pull DoS (seconds, no tools); wireless_local → RF jammer / 802.11 Deauth attack (no network access needed). Distinct from Exposure Level (the consequence) — location is the cause.

locationRationale.label: Location Rationale
locationRationale.placeholder: e.g. Field cable runs through public corridor → EL2 not EL1
locationRationale.helper: Required when physical medium and exposure level deviate from the standard mapping
locationRationale.tooltip: Justify deviations from the standard location→ExposureLevel mapping. IEC 62443-4-1: documented rationale required for audit traceability.

redundancy.label: Redundancy / Fallback

options.failover: Failover — automatic switch to backup path
options.degraded: Degraded — system continues with reduced functionality
options.buffered: Buffered — local buffer bridges short interruptions

redundancy.tooltip: System behaviour when this flow is interrupted. Drives DoS impact: 'none' + field_cable = Critical DoS (plug-pull stops the flow, no fallback). 'degraded' = device keeps running but loses that communication path.

tooltips.public: Freely shareable — no confidentiality protection required
tooltips.internal: Internal use only — not for external parties
tooltips.confidential: Restricted distribution — needs encryption in transit

dataTypeNotes.label: Data Type Notes
dataTypeNotes.placeholder: e.g. Proprietary telemetry frame, mixed sensor + status

tooltips.continuous: Uninterrupted stream — analog signals, video feeds
tooltips.periodic: Regular polling interval — Modbus, HART, SCADA cycles
tooltips.ondemand: Request-triggered — HTTP, OPC UA, database queries
tooltips.batch: Bulk transfer at intervals — file sync, log upload
tooltips.event_based: Triggered by state change — dry contact, alarm, MQTT publish

safetyRelevant.label: Carries safety-relevant data / supports safety function (EN 50742)

crossesSafetyBoundary.hint: This flow crosses a safety boundary (one side safety-relevant, other not). Extra scrutiny required for Tampering and Information Disclosure.

safetyRationale.label: Safety Rationale
safetyRationale.placeholder: e.g. Carries sensor data used by emergency stop logic
safetyRationale.error: Rationale required for custom safety function

integrityProtection.label: Integrity Protection (Checksums, Signatures)

options.crc: CRC — detects transmission errors, NOT targeted manipulation
options.hash: Hash (SHA-256) — detects changes, no key required

integrityProtection.tooltip: How is the integrity of stored data protected? CRC is NOT cryptographic — an attacker can recompute it after manipulation. Only HMAC and Signature provide tamper-resistance.

warnings.weak_integrity: CRC or no integrity protection — Tampering threat active (undetected manipulation possible)

storedDataTypes.label: Stored Data Types
storedDataTypes.placeholder: e.g. User credentials, Transaction logs, Configuration

accessControlMechanism.label: Access Control Mechanism
accessControlMechanism.tooltip: Technical mechanism enforcing access to this store. A DataStore is passive — enforcement always lives in a guarding Process or hardware. Complements the Access Control Policy field below.

accessControl.label: Access Control Policy
accessControl.placeholder: Which processes may read/write and under what conditions?
accessControl.tooltip: Policy description: which processes or actors have read/write access and under what conditions. Complements Access Control Mechanism (the how) with the who and when.

deletionPolicy.label: Deletion Mechanism
deletionPolicy.tooltip: Technical mechanism for secure data deletion. Note: overwrite on Flash is unreliable due to wear-leveling — prefer crypto_erase when encryptionAtRest is set. Complements the Deletion Policy field below.
deletionPolicy.placeholder: e.g. Soft delete with 30-day retention, GDPR-compliant

accessModel.label: Access Model
accessModel.tooltip: How is this store accessed? Direct Access = passive memory/storage with no responding actor (read/write). Communication = an active service that answers requests (pull). Derived from Technology by default; override with a rationale.

accessModelRationale.label: Access Model Rationale
accessModelRationale.placeholder: Why the access model deviates from the technology default
accessModelRationale.tooltip: Required when accessModel deviates from the technology default (IEC 62443-4-1 audit trail). Example: in-process SQLite file tagged as database → direct_access.

safetyRationale.label: Safety Rationale
safetyRationale.placeholder: e.g. Manipulation could disable emergency stop function

warnings.classification_no_encryption: Data classified as SECRET/RESTRICTED without encryption at rest — high Information Disclosure risk
warnings.safety_no_integrity: Safety-relevant data without integrity protection — Tampering threat (EN 50742)

warning.title: Trust Boundaries are critical!
warning.hint: Any data flow crossing this boundary requires extra scrutiny for all STRIDE threats.

tooltips.network: Separates network segments, e.g. DMZ from internal LAN or VPC from public internet
tooltips.privilege: Separates privilege levels, e.g. user space from kernel or admin from standard user
tooltips.organization: Separates organizational units, e.g. supplier from manufacturer or subsidiary from parent
tooltips.cloud: Separates cloud accounts, tenants or subscriptions with distinct IAM policies
tooltips.physical: Physical enclosure or cabinet boundary, e.g. machine housing or control panel
tooltips.legal: Regulatory or contractual boundary, e.g. GDPR data residency or PCI-DSS scope
tooltips.device: Boundary of a single device or embedded system, e.g. PLC, ECU or IoT gateway
tooltips.platform: Separates an app's own sandbox from a component controlled by the OS/platform vendor, e.g. a mobile OS browser broker or keychain/keystore. Same device, different responsible party — mitigations here rely on platform guarantees, not on your own code.
tooltips.peripheral: Boundary between MCU and external chips (SPI/I2C sensors, EEPROM, co-processors). Often overlooked attack surface.
tooltips.boot: Boundary between bootloader and application. Critical for firmware integrity and secure boot chain.
tooltips.debug: SWD, JTAG or UART console interface. Must be disabled or locked in production builds.

exposureLevel.helper: Defines the exposure level of this security zone. Elements with a higher EL are not affected.

tooltips.data_diode: Hardware data diode — unidirectional enforcement (IEC 62443 SL3+)
tooltips.authentication_gateway: Identity and authentication enforcement at boundary
tooltips.jump_host: Bastion / jump server for administrative access
tooltips.os_authentication: Device authentication (Face ID/Touch ID/biometric or passcode) is required before the OS releases the protected secret from Keychain/Keystore — distinct from authentication_gateway, which enforces identity at a network/API boundary.
tooltips.custom: Vendor or domain-specific — describe in Additional Controls

customBoundaryControls.label: Additional Controls
customBoundaryControls.placeholder: e.g. Siemens SCALANCE S615, OPC UA Reverse Proxy with allowlist
customBoundaryControls.helper: Vendor-specific or domain-specific controls not in the list above

securityAssumptions.label: Security Assumptions
securityAssumptions.placeholder: e.g. Inside is trusted, outside is hostile
securityAssumptions.helper: What do you assume about each side of this boundary?

boundaryControls.label: Controls at Boundary
boundaryControls.placeholder: e.g. Firewall, API Gateway, Authentication Layer

complianceRelevance.label: Compliance Relevance
complianceRelevance.placeholder: e.g. GDPR, ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, IEC 62443
complianceRelevance.helper: Which regulations apply to this boundary?

options.fail_close: Fail Close (no traffic on mechanism failure)

tooltips.allow_all: No traffic restriction — all zone-crossing flows permitted. NDR 5.2 RE(1) not satisfied.
tooltips.deny_all_permit_exception: Whitelist-based — only explicitly permitted flows pass. NDR 5.2 RE(1) satisfied.
tooltips.island_mode: Boundary can fully isolate the zone on security incident. NDR 5.2 RE(2) satisfied.
tooltips.fail_close: On mechanism failure: no traffic passes (fail-safe). NDR 5.2 RE(3) satisfied.

warning.title: Hardware boundary — physical attack surface!
warning.hint: Debug interfaces, firmware protection, and supply chain trust must be explicitly verified before production release.

tooltips.mcu: Microcontroller — STM32, NXP, Renesas. Threats: JTAG access, firmware tampering, secure boot bypass.
tooltips.som: System-on-Module — Toradex, RPi CM, Variscite. Supply chain trust especially relevant.
tooltips.fpga: Field Programmable Gate Array. Threats: bitstream tampering, readback, partial reconfiguration.
tooltips.dsp: Digital Signal Processor. Threat profile similar to MCU.
tooltips.se: Secure Element — ATECC608. Hardware-backed key storage, non-extractable by design.
tooltips.hsm: Hardware Security Module. Highest hardware assurance. Verify FIPS 140-2 or CC EAL4+ certification.

tooltips.none: No debug interface present or fully disabled. Recommended for production firmware.
tooltips.jtag: Full JTAG — CPU halt, memory access, flash read/write. Highest risk if not locked via fuse/OTP before production release.
tooltips.swd: SWD (ARM Serial Wire Debug) — similar capabilities to JTAG with fewer pins. Must be locked via RDP or equivalent before production release.
tooltips.jtag_trace: JTAG with ETM Trace Port — full instruction trace via parallel port. Requires separate physical connector (Mictor). Threat: complete code-flow disclosure.
tooltips.swd_swo: SWD with Single Wire Output — lightweight software trace via ITM. Single additional pin. Threat: software-generated trace messages readable.
tooltips.custom: Proprietary or vendor-specific debug interface. Document access method and locking mechanism in notes.

debugInterfaceLocked.label: Debug interface locked / disabled in production (Fuse / OTP)

tooltips.none: No protection — firmware readable and replaceable.
tooltips.rdp_level1: STM32 RDP1: readback disabled, debug limited.
tooltips.rdp_level2: STM32 RDP2: JTAG fully disabled, mass erase on tamper.
tooltips.encrypted: Firmware image is encrypted at rest.

tooltips.basic: Enclosure seal, tamper-evident label, or potting.
tooltips.active: Active tamper detection: voltage glitch, temperature, or mesh.

warning.title: Physical boundary — attack surface modelling!
warning.hint: Interfaces that cross or lie inside this boundary inherit its physical access preconditions. Verify tamper protection and access control before deployment.

tooltips.device_enclosure: Device housing — requires tool access (screws, hex key) to open. Typical for embedded devices, control units, sensors.
tooltips.cabinet: Lockable enclosure such as a Schaltschrank or server rack. Key or badge access.
tooltips.room: Access-controlled room such as a server room, production hall, or control room. Badge or key access.
tooltips.building: Building or facility perimeter. Highest-level physical boundary in most OT deployments.
tooltips.vehicle: Vehicle, machine, or mobile plant. Physical access controlled by enclosure or cab.
tooltips.tamper_zone: Sealed zone with active tamper protection — potting, tamper bag, or conductive mesh. No access without destruction.
tooltips.custom: Proprietary or non-standard physical boundary type. Describe in notes.

options.controlled: Controlled — key, badge, or PIN required

tooltips.public: No barrier — freely reachable (lobby, outdoor installation, public area). Maximum attacker exposure.
tooltips.controlled: Access restricted by a mechanism (key, badge, PIN). Role-based entry.
tooltips.guarded: Manned and monitored entry — active human presence at the boundary.
tooltips.sealed: Deprecated — use PEL0 + tamperProtection instead. Sealed is a tamper property, not an environmental context.

tooltips.none: No physical access control mechanism present.
tooltips.key: Mechanical key — standard or high-security cylinder.
tooltips.badge: RFID/NFC badge without second factor. Cloneable — relay attack risk applies.
tooltips.badge_pin: Badge plus PIN — mitigates relay attack and card sharing risk.
tooltips.biometric: Biometric authentication (fingerprint, iris) — strongest single physical factor.
tooltips.guard: Manned entry — identity checked by security personnel.

tooltips.none: No tamper protection — opening the boundary leaves no trace.
tooltips.seal: Tamper-evident label or seal — provides post-hoc evidence of opening, but does not prevent access.
tooltips.switch: Microswitch that triggers on enclosure opening — generates alert or interrupts power.
tooltips.mesh: Conductive mesh embedded in enclosure — cutting or drilling triggers detection.
tooltips.potting: Epoxy potting — no rework possible without destroying the board. Highest passive protection.
tooltips.active_detection: Voltage, temperature, or light sensor with automatic zeroize response — HSM / payment terminal level.

tooltips.none: No monitoring — attacker can operate undetected. Generates Repudiation threat.
tooltips.camera: CCTV or IP camera — post-hoc evidence only. Does not prevent access or trigger response.
tooltips.alarm: Motion or door alarm — real-time alert, but no active response capability.
tooltips.soc: Alarm routed to Security Operations Centre — active response capability.
tooltips.guard_patrol: Periodic manned patrol — detection window depends on patrol interval.
tooltips.tamper_monitoring: Electronic tamper sensor (switch, mesh, voltage) — often paired with zeroize response on adjacent Chip Boundary.

requiresToolAccess.label: Requires tool access to open (screwdriver, hex key)

tooltips.fixed: Device is permanently installed. Attacker must operate on-site under time pressure with limited tools. Offline lab attacks and device substitution are not applicable.
tooltips.removable: Device can be extracted with some effort (DIN-Rail clip, screws, connector). Enables Depot Attack, Maintenance Abuse, Hardware Swap. Attacker needs physical access and time for extraction.
tooltips.portable: Device can be carried away. Attacker gains full control of attack environment — unlimited time, lab equipment, Fault Injection, Side-Channel, Chip-Off, Firmware Implant. Critical: if safetyRelevant=true, generates Rogue Calibration and Safety-Critical Implant threats.
tooltips.vehicle_mounted: Device is installed in a vehicle and moves with it. Mobile but not hand-carried. Enables vehicle theft scenario and depot attack during maintenance windows.
